# @alexify/protoarray

> Zero-dependency, schema-based serialization for Node.js and browsers. Objects travel as
> positional JSON arrays (`{ name: 'Alex', age: 27 }` becomes `['Alex', 27]`), and a schema shared by
> the client and the server maps every position back to its key. A lightweight alternative to
> Protocol Buffers, maintained by Alexis Technologies.

Key facts:
- Package (npm): `@alexify/protoarray`, installed with `npm install @alexify/protoarray`
- Node.js >= 18 and browsers; CommonJS with ESM named-import interop; hand-written `index.d.ts`
  with `Infer<D>` and `Input<D>` inferred from the definition literal
- Zero runtime dependencies, no build step, about 20 KB min+gzip for the core; subpaths
  `/registry`, `/stream`, `/metaschema` and `/standalone` add 0.4–2 KB each
- The payload is plain JSON: about 45% smaller than keyed objects before compression, and faster
  to parse and stringify (×1.5 encode, ×1.7 decode on a typical record in V8)
- Definition DSL is `@alexify/metaschema`'s: `'string'`, `'?number'`, `'key?'`, `'integer'`,
  `'any'`, `'unknown'`, `'null'`, nested structs, `{ array: T }`, `{ set: T }`, `{ map: { K: V } }`,
  `{ object: { string: V } }`, `{ enum: [...] }`, `{ flags: [...] }`, `{ union: [...],
  discriminator }`, `'date'`, `'bigint'`, `'bytes'`, `'json'`, tuples of any elements,
  `{ type, required, default, decimals, aliases, delta, intern }`, schemas by value or by name
- Wire rules: one field per position in declaration order; missing/undefined/null travel as null;
  trailing nulls are trimmed; enum → index, date → epoch ms, bigint → decimal string, bytes →
  base64, decimals → scaled integer, flags → bitmask (an array of 31-bit words past 31 names),
  union → `[tag, ...branch fields]`; `{ sparse: true }` → `[mask, ...present]` per 31 fields;
  collections as rows, `flat` or `columns`; set → array, map → `[k0, v0, …]`; `delta: true` →
  first value and differences; `intern` → `[table, body]` with strings as table indexes
- Schema evolution: append fields at the end, never reorder; older and newer versions interoperate;
  `schema.id` fingerprints the canonical form (FNV-1a 32-bit, or the `fingerprint` option);
  `Schema.resolve(writer, reader)` reads and writes another version by name (aliases, renames,
  widening); `SchemaRegistry` (`/registry`) keeps schemas by id and wraps payloads `[id, payload]`
- Two backends: generated code (`new Function`) by default, composed closures where code
  generation is blocked (CSP without unsafe-eval, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge); standalone
  modules (`/standalone`, `protoarray compile`) carry generated code to such runtimes
- Streaming (`/stream`): `encodeEach`/`decodeEach`, NDJSON, `TransformStream`s, the items of a large
  JSON array read as they arrive
- metaschema (`/metaschema`): `fromMetaschema`, `fromModel`, custom `types` for `bytes`/`flags`
- Validation: `validate: true` (default) or `'decode'` checks the wire on decode and trusts the
  values given to encode, `'both'` checks the values too, `'encode'` only them, `false` neither;
  `EncodeError` and `DecodeError` with `code`, `path` (`orders[1].sku`) and `schema`;
  `schema.check(value)` returns the `EncodeError` a validated encode would throw, or `null`,
  whatever the mode; `SchemaDefinitionError` for a broken definition
- Exports: `Schema`, `encode`, `decode`, `stringify`, `parse`, `check`, `encodeEach`,
  `decodeEach`, `SchemaDefinitionError`, `EncodeError`, `DecodeError`
- wrpc: a union of wrpc's packet types makes a packet codec (https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/wrpc)
- Docs: https://protoarray.vercel.app/ (guide, wire format, benchmarks, API reference)
